# 1. Dataset Identification and Rationale

We use the built-in `mtcars` dataset in R. 
**Rationale:** The `mtcars` dataset is clean, structured, and ideal for predictive modeling. We aim to predict car fuel efficiency (`mpg` - Miles Per Gallon) using predictor variables such as vehicle weight (`wt`) and horsepower (`hp`). This allows us to apply multiple linear regression effectively.

```{r load-data}
# Load dataset and view first few rows
data(mtcars)
head(mtcars)

# Summary statistics for selected variables
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])

# Correlation matrix
cor(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])

# Normality test (Shapiro-Wilk test on mpg)
shapiro.test(mtcars$mpg)

set.seed(123)

# Train/Test Split
train_index <- sample(1:nrow(mtcars), 0.8 * nrow(mtcars))
train_data <- mtcars[train_index, ]
test_data <- mtcars[-train_index, ]

# Fit Multiple Linear Regression Model
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = train_data)
summary(model)

# Diagnostic plots for residuals
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Predictions on test data
predictions <- predict(model, newdata = test_data)

# Calculate RMSE
rmse <- sqrt(mean((test_data$mpg - predictions)^2))
print(paste("Test RMSE:", rmse))
